QuestionRequestFollow-up

When the database and cache both change, how do you keep them consistent?

Suggested answerStreaming

We update the database first, then delete the cache. Failed deletes go to a retry queue, and a Canal binlog subscriber deletes again as a safety net; hot keys get a delayed double delete.

    01 · Job interview

    The follow-up,handled.

    The interviewer presses on cache consistency. In the bar under your camera, the answer is already forming, built on a project from your résumé.

    Floating teleprompter · click-through · hide with ⌘⇧\

    02 · Academic talk

    Your notes turnwith the slides.

    Points tick off as you cover them, and the next transition is ready. When someone cuts in, the explanation cites its page.

    Pick a window, display or region · each answer keeps its frame

    03 · Negotiation

    They push on price.You hold your floor.

    They ask for another eight percent. It suggests a tiered offer within the floor you set for this meeting, and notes decisions and to-dos.

    Phone companion on the table · paired by QR, off by default

    04 · Online class

    Called on,and composed.

    Asked what happens on a TLB miss, the answer follows lecture 9, slide 23. A question or code on screen can be cropped and asked.

    Ask with a screenshot · aligned to the slides

    05 · Afterwards

    After the call,the notes are done.

    A summary, the questions and the material used are filed under the scene. Good answers are kept; weak ones return in the next review.

    Searchable · export to Markdown · delete any time

    № 03Phone companion

    Sharing your screen?
    Read your phone.

    1. i.You’re sharing your whole screen.

      Whatever is on your Mac, they see.

    2. ii.One scan, and the phone is in.

      The camera reads the code; the browser becomes your prompter. No app.

    3. iii.Questions and answers, on the phone only.

      Nothing new on the shared screen. Only this moment syncs; transcripts and material stay on the Mac.

    № 04Privacy

    What stays on your Mac,
    and what leaves.

    1. i.

      Your voice stays on this Mac.

      Speech is recognised on your Mac and raw audio is never saved. Cloud recognition is used only if you agree to it.

    2. ii.

      Only the passages that matter.

      Answers use only the passages retrieved for the question at hand, not your whole library. Material and records stay on your Mac.

    3. iii.

      You decide what leaves.

      Answers go through the service you choose, and its key stays in your Keychain; web search and the phone companion are off by default.

    No stealth promises: get consent before recording, and follow the rules of the room. Full data notes
